subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Use communication verbs: explain, mean, pronounce, repeat, translate, understand.
Choose correctly between tell/talk, say/speak and hear/listen.
Use verbs with the right prepositions, like talk to and listen to.

tf.s: 'Translate' means change words into another language.
tf.why: We translate from one language into another.

tf.s: We say 'I said him that he was wrong.'
tf.why: We say something to someone: 'I said to him ...' or 'I told him ...'.

tf.s: We say 'tell someone something', like 'Tell me a story.'
tf.why: Tell is followed directly by the person.

tf.s: We say 'We say two languages at home.'
tf.why: We speak languages: 'We speak two languages at home.'

tf.s: 'Can you listen me now?' is correct.
tf.why: Listen needs 'to'; here we need hear: 'Can you hear me now?'

tf.s: 'Pronounce' means say a word with the correct sounds.
tf.why: For example: How do you pronounce 'quiet'?
'Could you repeat it, please?' asks someone to say it again.

tf.s: We say 'talk to your friends about your problems'.
'Explain' means change words into another language.
tf.why: Explain means make something clear; translate changes the language.

tf.s: Gestures, pictures and translation apps can help people communicate without a shared language.
tf.why: These were ideas from the lesson discussion.

boxes.q: Choose: She didn't ___ me the answer.
Complete: I didn't catch that. Could you ___ it, please?
Complete: How do you ___ this word?
boxes.why: Pronounce is about the sound of a word.
We ask what a word means.

boxes.q: Complete: Sometimes she ___ Spanish to me.
Complete: I ask my Thai friend to ___ for me.
boxes.why: He changes Thai into my language.

o: Can you hear to me now?

boxes.q: Complete: Can you ___ how this machine works?
Choose: Do you ___ to your friends about problems?

hunt.q: Say the sounds of a word

mcq.q: Which verb means 'have a definition or explanation'?
mcq.why: We ask: What does this word mean?
Say something to someone; tell someone something.

mcq.q: Which verb is NOT followed by 'to' before a person?
mcq.why: We tell someone directly: tell me.

mcq.q: Which verb is about sound you notice without trying?
mcq.why: We hear sounds; we listen when we pay attention.

mcq.q: Complete: You can't read a menu in Thai, so your friend ___ it into English for you.
mcq.why: Changing a menu into English is translating.

o: He told me that he was tired.
He said me that he was tired.
He talked me that he was tired.
He spoke me that he was tired.

mcq.q: Your friend speaks very fast and you don't understand. What do you say?
mcq.why: Asking someone to repeat is polite and clear.

mcq.q: Why is 'Can you listen me now?' wrong?
o: Listen needs 'to', and here we really mean hear
mcq.why: On a phone call we ask: Can you hear me?

o: I speak Arabic, and I say 'hello' to my teacher.
I say Arabic, and I speak 'hello' to my teacher.
I speak Arabic, and I say my teacher hello.
I say Arabic, and I tell 'hello'.
mcq.why: Speak a language; say words to someone.

mcq.q: You meet a visitor who doesn't speak your language. Which is the best way to communicate?
o: Use gestures, pictures or a translation app, and be patient
mcq.why: Patience and helpful tools make communication easier.
